note: North Korea's citizen's identity card is issued on reaching the age of majority, 17 (NK News, 17 October 2017); cards are renewed in nationwide re-issues, the latest begun in 2017 with photographs of all residents of 17 and over, and delayed (Asiapress, 17 January 2019). Its fee, term and time aren't known from any source read.

sources.title: NK News, Papers, please: North Korea's identification cards (17 October 2017)
sources.said: This is a standard identity document for a North Korean citizen, issued when one reaches the age of majority. Unlike most countries, in North Korea this age is not 18, but 17 ... All citizens have to bear IDs issued by the police

sources.title: Asiapress, North Korea renews nationality cards (17 January 2019)
sources.said: The process for the renewal of identity cards began in 2017, with the authorities announcing that new cards would be issued in May 2018. By the end of 2017, photographs had been taken of all residents aged 17 and older.
